# QS-CFW-5753-95 Quality specification - track link CFW-5753-95 (15B37)

Revision: Rev A  
Plant: P2  
Parts: CFW-5753-95

Scope
- This quality specification applies to forged track link CFW-5753-95 (CFW-5753-95) produced at Plant P2 and is the controlling document for final acceptance of material, dimensional conformity, hardness, and weight prior to release to assembly or inventory.
- The document covers acceptance criteria, inspection methods, rationale for test choices, examples of typical nonconformances, and records to be retained in the document control system for traceability.
- It is intended for use by quality engineers, inspectors, forging operations, heat treat, and shipping personnel when verifying and releasing track links.

Requirements table
| Feature | Requirement | Acceptance |
|---|---:|---|
| Hardness (through hardened area) | 34-37 HRC | Accept only parts with hardness within 34-37 HRC across specified measurement locations. |
| Bore diameter | Per drawing with bore diameter tolerance of ±0.03 mm | Accept only parts where measured bore diameter is within drawing specification and the stated tolerance of ±0.03 mm. |
| Forging weight (maximum) | Maximum forging weight 28.3 kg | Reject parts that exceed the maximum forging weight of 28.3 kg as received from the forge operation. |

Notes on table
- The hardness range for track link CFW-5753-95 (CFW-5753-95) is critical to wear life and must be verified after applicable thermal processing. Hardness readings outside the range indicate a process deviation requiring containment and investigation.
- The bore diameter tolerance for track link CFW-5753-95 (CFW-5753-95) is ±0.03 mm and must be confirmed against the nominal dimension shown on the controlled drawing referenced in the work order.
- The maximum forging weight for track link CFW-5753-95 (CFW-5753-95) is 28.3 kg; material exceeding this mass suggests an overforge condition or material inclusion and must not be released.

Inspection method
- Visual inspection: Inspect each part for forging defects that could affect fit or function, such as laps, cold shuts, cracks, and significant surface inclusions. Use magnification as required to confirm suspected discontinuities. Parts with suspected internal discontinuities shall be segregated pending further nondestructive evaluation.
- Dimensional inspection: Verify bore diameter at specified locations using calibrated bore gauges or coordinate measuring equipment capable of reading to the specified drawing resolution. Compare measurements directly to the nominal drawing dimension and the bore diameter tolerance of ±0.03 mm. Record measured values on the inspection record.
- Hardness testing: Perform hardness testing on the through-hardened area using a calibrated Rockwell hardness tester set to the appropriate scale. Take measurements at the specified locations detailed on the inspection drawing. The hardness range for track link CFW-5753-95 (CFW-5753-95) is 34-37 HRC; parts must exhibit values within this range. If hardness readings vary across locations, record all readings and hold the lot until disposition is determined.
- Weight verification: Weigh each forging on a calibrated scale to confirm the forging weight does not exceed the maximum forging weight 28.3 kg. For batches where full-piece weighing is not practical, perform representative checks and escalate to 100 percent weighing if any sample exceeds the maximum.
- Nondestructive testing: Where indicated by process control or suspect indications from visual inspection, perform magnetic particle inspection or ultrasonic testing per the applicable procedure. Record results and attach to the inspection log.

Rationale and examples
- Hardness rationale: Maintaining hardness within 34-37 HRC ensures a balance between wear resistance and fracture toughness. For example, a part hardened above the specified range may be brittle under impact; a part below may wear prematurely in service.
- Bore tolerance rationale: The bore tolerance of ±0.03 mm controls fit with mating pins and affects assembly preload and track articulation. An out-of-tolerance bore can produce premature wear or assembly interference.
- Weight rationale: The maximum forging weight 28.3 kg guards against excessive material that can indicate incorrect die fill, excessive flash, or material defects. For example, an over-weight forging may not properly heat treat or may contain hidden inclusions that compromise integrity.

Nonconformance handling
- Segregation: Immediately segregate any part or lot that fails to meet any requirement in the table. Mark segregation tags with the part number, lot identifier, and the failed feature(s).
- Containment: Halt release of the affected lot. Notify quality engineering and production supervision. Suspend downstream process operations for affected serials or batches until disposition is set by quality engineering.
- Investigation: Quality engineering will review production records, heat treat records, tool maintenance logs, and inspection records to determine root cause. For hardness deviations, review heat treat cycle data and quench medium condition. For bore deviations, review die maintenance and machining records. For weight exceedance, review forging parameters and die design confirmation.
- Disposition: Options include rework if technically feasible, reheat/temper only when approved by engineering, scrapping, or use-as-is with engineering acceptance for minor deviations that do not affect safety or function. Any use-as-is disposition requires written engineering approval filed with the inspection record.
- Examples of disposition scenarios:
  - A single part with a bore out of tolerance due to machining error may be reworked if material and geometry permit; reworked parts must be re-inspected to confirm compliance with bore diameter tolerance of ±0.03 mm.
  - A lot with hardness below the specified range across multiple samples requires suspension of release and corrective action in the heat treat process; parts are not released until hardness is within 34-37 HRC.
  - Overweight forgings discovered at receipt from the forge should be quarantined and returned to forging operations for evaluation when weight exceeds the maximum forging weight 28.3 kg.

Records to keep
- Inspection log showing measured bore diameters and individual hardness readings for each inspected location, with identifiers linking parts to production lot and heat lot.
- Weight records from calibrated scales indicating measured forging weight versus the maximum forging weight 28.3 kg.
- Visual and nondestructive testing reports, including photographs of any suspect defects.
- Nonconformance reports, containment records, root cause analysis, corrective actions, and disposition approvals signed by quality engineering and production supervision.
- All records shall be retained in the document control system under the part identifier CFW-5753-95 for traceability and audit.

Revision control
- Maintain this document under version control. Any procedural changes that affect inspection methods or acceptance criteria for CFW-5753-95 must be approved by quality management and documented in the revision history.
